title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. X_· is a semi-simplicial set ("½ simplicial"). Grothendieck studies the functor F_X(M_·) = Hom_{Δ̂}(X_·, M_·) on (perfect) simplicial k-modules M_·. By Dold–Kan-type arguments this functor is controlled by the cochain complex C* = C*(X_·, k). The previous page states the main aim: to recover the multiplicative structure 'on top of' this functor. That structure consists of the cup-product maps F(M)⊗_k F(N) → F(M⊗N) and the divided-power maps Γ^i F(M) → F(Γ^i M), where Γ^i is applied degreewise. Both should be viewed as extra structure on C*.

This page continues as follows.
(1) When k is a field of characteristic 0 (presumably Q), these extra structures are determined by the De Rham–Sullivan complex of X, i.e. Sullivan's polynomial differential forms A_PL(X), a strictly commutative cdga.
(2) For arbitrary k (and in characteristic ≠ 0; 'the principle is the same') they are determined by 'De Rham complexes with divided powers'. These would be simplicial divided-power polynomial forms Γ_k[t_0..t_n] ⊗ Λ(dt_i) on the simplices, which satisfy a Poincaré lemma because divided powers allow integration.
(3) A parenthesis, corrected from 'définit' to 'rectifiant': C* with the extra structures envisaged 'rectifies' to the De Rham–Sullivan complexes, resp. the divided-power De Rham complexes. In modern terms, the homotopy-coherent (E∞ / divided-power) structure on cochains is strictified by a commutative (divided-power) dg model.
(4) The real question: to what extent does C* with its multiplicative structures with divided powers allow one to reconstruct the homotopy type of the X it comes from?
(5) A closing exclamation about 'many fascinating relations'.

The next page switches to a linear-algebra 'dévissage': a combinatorial description of perfect complexes via the additive category generated by the K(i).

So the page is a programmatic statement. It sets out a rational-homotopy-style reconstruction problem over arbitrary k, with divided-power (E∞-like) cochain structures replacing Sullivan's commutative forms.
errors: The claim 'il est clair' that, for general k (in particular in characteristic p), C* with its multiplicative / divided-power structure is rectified by a strictly (graded-)commutative divided-power De Rham complex cannot hold in that form.

Counterexample for (3): for k = F_2 and X = RP^∞, the generator a ∈ H^1 has a^2 ≠ 0. In a strictly graded-commutative model, odd elements (such as 1-forms with dt∧dt = 0) square to zero, so no such strict model exists. More generally, Steenrod operations are obstructions; only E∞ (or cosimplicial-algebra) models exist in positive characteristic.

There is also a technical gap. Simplicial divided-power polynomial forms on simplices in barycentric coordinates require divided powers of 1 − Σ t_i, i.e. γ_n(1) = 1/n!, which is undefined in characteristic p. Integral De Rham-type theories (Cenkl–Porter) needed cubical or filtered modifications.
Over Q the statement is correct (Sullivan), but the reconstruction of homotopy type then requires nilpotence / finite-type hypotheses, which the page does not mention.

ideas.what: Encode the multiplicative structure of cochains functorially via maps F(M)⊗F(N)→F(M⊗N) and Γ^i F(M)→F(Γ^i M), on the functor M ↦ Hom(X, M) from simplicial modules.
ideas.modern_name: E∞ / divided-power (cosimplicial commutative algebra) structure on cochains; polynomial-functor description of cochain algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod/May (operations), Hinich–Schechtman, Mandell (E∞ cochains), Toën (affine stacks)
ideas.where_published: Related ideas appear in the 1975 letter to Breen and in Pursuing Stacks (schematization of homotopy types); this specific functorial formulation is not known to me in published form.

missed.claim: An early (c. 1975–76) explicit formulation of the problem of reconstructing homotopy types over arbitrary k (including char p) from cochains equipped with divided-power multiplicative structure. It is framed via the functor M ↦ Hom(X,M) on perfect simplicial modules with Γ^i-operations, and anticipates Mandell's theorems and Toën's affine stacks.
missed.quote: il faut voir dans quelle mesure C* avec ses structures multiplicatives à p.d. permet de reconstituer le type d'homotopie du X dont il provient
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically this documents the origin of the schematization program in a concrete divided-power cochain form, contemporaneous with the Breen letter. The functor-of-points formulation on perfect complexes with Γ^i maps is close to modern 'cochains as algebras over polynomial-functor theories' approaches, e.g. derived binomial rings (Horel, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov 2023). It is mainly of historical rather than new mathematical value.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic note, not a result. It is interesting as an early, explicit divided-power version of the cochain-reconstruction / schematization question, predating Mandell and Toën. However, the theme is already known from Grothendieck's 1975 Breen letter and Pursuing Stacks, and the 'rectification' claim is incorrect in positive characteristic.
